The Hunt · art direction

Hand-drawn style lab

His face first (front three-quarter, friendly expression), then the portrait swing camera at address and at the finish. Same golfer, range and lighting throughout: each finish is a post-process over the realistic render, so proportions and swing stay real. Frames are the portrait swing camera on a phone. More dots means the finish hides more of the procedural texture and modelling, so the art needs less detail to look good.

0

Realistic (today)

The game as it renders now: tone-mapped and graded, no illustration.

What it hides
Nothing. Every texture and modelling flaw shows.
How much simpler the art gets
1

Coloured Pencil

Realistic proportions and soft light, drawn in coloured pencil on white paper: grain that fills in with the tone, directional hatching in the darks, a light brown contour.

What it hides
Skin and fabric texture flaws and blotchy shading; strokes carry the form like a hand-drawn portrait.
How much simpler the art gets
2

Graphic Realism · Light

The realistic render with a light hand-drawn finish: fine ink contours that swell and taper, a little hatching in the deepest shadows, faint paper grain.

What it hides
Blotchy fabric shading and texture noise; edges read cleaner. The face stays photographic.
How much simpler the art gets
3

Graphic Realism · Medium

Pushed further: stronger contours and interior lines, cross-hatching in shadows, crisper highlights, visible paper.

What it hides
Most fabric and turf texture flaws and some modelling softness. The face reads as a drawn portrait.
How much simpler the art gets
4

Graphic Novel

High-contrast colour, heavy cross-hatching in shadows and thick ink contours.

What it hides
Shadow noise and flat cloth; hatching adds form. Strongest drawn look of the realistic family.
How much simpler the art gets
5

Cover Art

Sports-game cover illustration: flat saturated colour in a few clean bands, black contours and a bright rim.

What it hides
Almost all texture; the face reads from its big features (hair, nose, jaw, smile).
How much simpler the art gets
6

Ink & Wash

A transparent watercolour wash over bold brown ink lines, colour floating slightly off the line work, cold-press paper.

What it hides
Skin and fabric texture, small seams, turf tiling.
How much simpler the art gets
7

Painterly

Big oil-paint strokes following the forms, canvas weave, a crisp edge on the golfer.

What it hides
Nearly all surface detail: cloth weave, hair strands, grass noise.
How much simpler the art gets
8

Sports Poster

Flat cel bands, heavy navy outlines and big halftone dots in the shadows.

What it hides
Texture detail and small shape errors.
How much simpler the art gets
9

Gouache

Opaque paint in four values, visible brush direction, a warm palette and paint-tinted outlines.

What it hides
Most texture and lighting noise; the face becomes a few planes of colour.
How much simpler the art gets
